**STEP 1 - Scene:** A breakfast tray with two slices of buttered-style toast on a paper plate, two butter portions, two jam portions, a mug of milky tea, and a colour calibration card.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A paper side plate, about 20 cm in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 10² ≈ 314 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** (1) two slices of toast, (2) two butter portions, (3) two jam portions. The mug of tea sits on the tray, not the plate, so I count it separately.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Toast covers about 55% of the plate. Butter and jam portions are small, about 3% and 2% of the plate.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Toast: 173 cm² × ~1.2 cm ≈ 208 ml. Butter and jam are small, roughly 15 ml and 25 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Toast is dry bread, so I use about 0.3 g/ml, which gives ~62 g. This is more realistic than the 0.9–1.0 bread-slice density, since two slices weigh about 60–70 g. Butter ≈ 14 g, jam ≈ 24 g. Tea with a splash of milk is about 200 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Toast ~270 kcal/100 g → ~168 kcal. Butter ~717 kcal/100 g → ~100 kcal. Jam ~250 kcal/100 g → ~60 kcal. Milky tea ~10 kcal/100 g → ~20 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Plate food totals about 86 g and about 330 kcal, which fits two slices of toast with a little spread. Adding the tea gives about 350 kcal.
